programDescription: Biomedical and software engineering is an integrated program that combines computing to solve, manage, and create smart technologies, and applies them through a biomedical lens to create technologies that connect and sustain the medical industry.Key topics include programming and software development, data structures and algorithms, Biomedical systems and human physiology, medical imaging and signal processing, artificial intelligence in healthcare, and health informatics and wearable tech
admissionCoursesNeeded:
English
Calculus and Vectors
Chemistry
Physics
Biology
academicCostDetails: Includes textbooks which are around 1-1.5k, orientation which is $114, student fees which are $1k per year
livingCostDetails: Includes Housing ranging from 9-12k, food which is 7k, entertainment which is 2-3k, transportation which is $252, all per year
interestingFacts: <ol> <li> The iBioMed program is one of the first of its kind in Canada, combining engineering and health sciences from year one. <li> Students can work on real medical technologies, like prosthetics or health-monitoring devices. <li> McMaster University is known for its problem-based learning approach, especially in health-related fields. <ol>
